title: ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml's classification_table has inconsistent counts and double-classifies 5 table names as both GLOBAL_REGISTRY and PER_TENANT
registered_by: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF03-GH566-20260808 Step 2b, incidental finding while validating a GBL-136 follow-up migration design)
related_to: ISS-0185 / GH #518 -- the diagnosis this file belongs to
ISS-0617 / GH #566 -- the run during which this was discovered

ISS-0620 / GH #573 -- a separate, more severe misclassification issue in the SAME diagnosis file (4 tables classified in the wrong direction entirely, causing already-executed data loss). This issue (ISS-0621) is about internal inconsistency/double-classification, not the wrong-direction problem ISS-0620 covers -- they are related but distinct defects in the same source document.
symptom: The classification_table section's global_registry_tenant_default_is_stray list is labeled ':37' but the actual YAML list beneath it contains 33 items. The per_tenant_public_is_stray list is labeled ':8' but actually contains 13 items. 33+13=46, not the file's own stated total_classified:45. Additionally, and more consequentially: 5 table names (api_token_audit, event_payload_store, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, variable_schemas) appear in BOTH lists simultaneously -- classified as GLOBAL_REGISTRY (public canonical, tenant_default is the stray shadow) in one list and as PER_TENANT (tenant_default canonical, public is the stray shadow) in the other, a direct logical contradiction for the same 5 names.
root_cause_analysis: Not traced to the exact authoring step that produced the double-classification (the diagnosis file does not record intermediate drafts). Operationally, the conflict was already resolved once in practice: migrations/GBL-135_iss0185_drop_per_tenant_shadows.sql's actual v_tables array includes all 5 of these disputed names and has already executed against the shared bpm_test database, dropping their public copies -- meaning GBL-135's author (or a later editor) treated these 5 as PER_TENANT and acted on that classification, while GBL-134's downstream consumers (including a rework of a later migration design during WF03-GH566-20260808) were still reading the diagnosis file's GLOBAL_REGISTRY list, which also claims these names, and would have produced a second, contradictory migration had CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR not caught the discrepancy against live database state before implementation.
impact: The diagnosis file is treated as an authoritative source for at least two already-merged migrations (GBL-134, GBL-135) and at least one in-progress follow-up (this run's GBL-136 design, currently under rework). An unresolved internal contradiction in the source-of-truth document creates a live risk that future migrations, tooling (e.g. tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py, if it also consumes this classification), or manual investigations will pick whichever list they happen to read first and act on a decision the file itself does not actually settle.
acceptance_criteria: The 5 double-classified table names (api_token_audit, event_payload_store, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, variable_schemas) are resolved to exactly one classification each, with the decision recorded and justified (recommend: PER_TENANT, matching what GBL-135 already executed, to avoid a second migration reversing already-applied production state -- but this should be explicitly verified, not assumed, against actual column shape / tenant_id presence per the diagnosis file's own stated classification method)
The classification_table's list labels (':37', ':8') are corrected to match actual list lengths, and total_classified/total_observed are reconciled to the corrected counts
tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py is checked to confirm it does not also encode the double-classification or the stale counts
Any other consumer of this diagnosis file (existing migrations, in-progress designs) is checked for whether it relied on the now-corrected classification for any of these 5 names
evidence_file: Found and verified during CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's review of src/design/iss0617-gbl134-missing-tables-followup.md (WF03-GH566-20260808 Step 2b) -- see that handoff's result.issues for the live psql verification queries against bpm_test confirming GBL-135 already dropped the 5 disputed names' public copies.
notes: Discovered incidentally while validating an unrelated migration design (GBL-136, itself a follow-up to complete GBL-134's incomplete table coverage for GH-566/ISS-0617). Not fixed in that run -- filed separately per the incidental-discovery protocol. The immediate practical consequence for GH-566's own GBL-136 design (these 5 names should likely be excluded from its scope, since GBL-135 already resolved them PER_TENANT) is being handled as part of that design's rework, but the underlying source-document inconsistency this issue tracks is broader than just GBL-136's needs and deserves its own resolution.
